categories.name: PET plastic
categories.summary: Clear drink and food bottles marked with resin code 1.
steps: Empty the bottle completely
Rinse it quickly
Put the cap back on
Place it in the plastics bin

categories.name: HDPE plastic
categories.summary: Milk jugs, detergent and shampoo bottles marked with resin code 2.
steps: Empty the container
Rinse out any residue
Keep the cap on
Place it in the plastics bin

categories.name: PVC plastic
categories.summary: Pipes, cling wrap and some packaging marked with resin code 3.
steps: Check with your local collector: PVC is often not accepted
Remove any food or liquid residue
Keep it apart from other plastics
If not accepted, use the general waste bin

categories.name: LDPE plastic
categories.summary: Soft film such as shopping bags and wrap, resin code 4.
steps: Shake out any contents
Keep film plastic separate from rigid plastic
Bundle bags together inside one bag
Take it to a film collection point if available

categories.name: PP plastic
categories.summary: Food tubs, bottle caps and straws marked with resin code 5.
steps: Empty the tub
Rinse off food residue
Place it in the plastics bin

categories.name: PS plastic
categories.summary: Foam trays, cups and disposable cutlery marked with resin code 6.
steps: Check with your local collector: PS is often not accepted
Remove food residue
Do not crush foam into small pieces
If not accepted, use the general waste bin

categories.name: Other plastic
categories.summary: Mixed or multi-layer plastics marked with resin code 7.
steps: Check the label for a more specific type
Empty and rinse it
Ask your local collector whether code 7 is accepted

categories.name: Plastic (type unknown)
categories.summary: Plastic item where the resin type cannot be told from the photo.
steps: Look for the resin code (a number 1 to 7) on the bottom
Empty and rinse the item
Put it in the plastics bin if it is a clean rigid item
Film plastic goes separately

categories.name: Paper
categories.summary: Office paper, newspapers, magazines and clean paper bags.
steps: Keep it dry and clean
Remove plastic covers and staples if easy
Place it in the paper bin

categories.name: Cardboard
categories.summary: Shipping boxes and corrugated packaging.
steps: Remove tape and labels
Flatten the box
Keep it dry
Greasy parts, such as pizza box bottoms, go to general waste

categories.name: Beverage carton
categories.summary: Milk and juice cartons made of layered paper, plastic and foil.
steps: Empty the carton
Rinse and let it dry
Flatten it and put the cap back
Place it in the paper bin or a carton collection point

categories.name: Glass
categories.summary: Glass bottles and jars.
steps: Empty and rinse the container
Remove metal lids and caps
Do not add ceramics, mirrors or light bulbs
Wrap broken glass in paper before disposal
warnings: Broken glass can cut: wrap it and handle it with care.

categories.name: Aluminum
categories.summary: Drink cans, foil trays and aluminum lids.
steps: Empty the can
Rinse it
Crush it if you can to save space
Place it in the metals bin

categories.name: Steel
categories.summary: Food cans, tools and steel containers.
steps: Empty and rinse food cans
Remove paper labels if easy
Place small items in the metals bin
Take large items to a scrap metal collector

categories.name: Other metal
categories.summary: Copper, brass and mixed scrap metal.
steps: Remove any plastic or rubber parts
Collect it separately from other waste
Sell or give it to a scrap metal collector

categories.name: Food waste
categories.summary: Leftovers, peels, coffee grounds and spoiled food.
steps: Remove packaging and plastic
Drain extra liquid
Place it in the organic bin or compost
Do not pour cooking oil into the bin

categories.name: Garden waste
categories.summary: Leaves, grass clippings and small branches.
steps: Remove plastic bags and ties
Cut long branches into short pieces
Compost it or use the organic bin

categories.name: Small electronics
categories.summary: Phones, chargers, cables, remote controls and small gadgets.
steps: Remove batteries and dispose of them separately
Delete personal data from devices
Never put it in the general bin
Take it to an e-waste collection point
warnings: Electronics contain toxic materials. Check your local authorities for collection points.

categories.name: Large appliances
categories.summary: Fridges, washing machines, TVs and computers.
steps: Do not break or open the appliance
Keep it dry and upright
Arrange a pickup or a drop-off at an e-waste point
Ask the seller about take-back offers
warnings: Fridges and ACs contain gases that harm the environment. Check your local authorities.

categories.name: Batteries
categories.summary: Household, button and rechargeable batteries.
steps: Tape the terminals of lithium and 9V batteries
Store them in a dry non-metal container
Never put them in the general bin
Take them to a battery collection point
warnings: Batteries can start fires and leak toxic chemicals. Do not crush or burn them. Check your local authorities.

categories.name: Textiles
categories.summary: Clothes, shoes, bedding and fabric.
steps: Donate items that are clean and wearable
Bag worn or torn items separately
Take them to a textile recycling point

categories.name: Hazardous chemicals
categories.summary: Paint, solvents, pesticides, motor oil and cleaning chemicals.
steps: Keep it in the original container
Do not mix different chemicals
Never pour it down a drain or onto the ground
Take it to a hazardous waste collection point
warnings: Can be toxic, flammable or corrosive. Keep away from children and heat. Check your local authorities.

categories.name: Medical waste
categories.summary: Sharps, expired medication and used masks.
steps: Put needles and sharps in a rigid, closed container
Return unused medication to a pharmacy
Seal used masks in a bag
Never put sharps loose in the bin
warnings: Sharps and medication can injure or poison people. Check your local authorities for safe disposal.

categories.name: Wood
categories.summary: Clean wood, pallets and furniture parts.
steps: Remove nails and metal parts
Reuse or donate it if possible
Collect painted or treated wood separately
Take it to a wood collection point

categories.name: Construction waste
categories.summary: Rubble, bricks, tiles and plasterboard.
steps: Keep it separate from household waste
Sort metal and wood out first
Arrange a skip or collection service
Do not leave it on public land

categories.name: General waste
categories.summary: Items that cannot be recycled, reused or composted.
steps: Check that no recycling bin fits the item
Bag it securely
Place it in the general waste bin
